procedure.method: Fresh independent portfolio critic; no spawn, fork, resume, peer review, producer self-inspection or unlisted embedded-path access. Verified the exact pinned document bytes; read packet, case, review rules, rubric, recording README/addendum/adapter and ratio policy, then read all five pinned native-evidence manifests and verified the exact image pins and PNG dimensions. The packet has no source assets and no protected layouts. Actually opened and visually inspected, using tools.view_image detail original and image emission detail original, M1 native/usage720/thumbnail320, then M2 native/usage720/thumbnail320, M3 native/usage720/thumbnail320, M4 native/usage720/thumbnail320 and M5 native/usage720/thumbnail320: all 15 exact poster views preceded the first copy-reading/transcription stage, judgment or score. Usage views are 720×405, thumbnails 320×180; native dimensions are those in the packet. Retained 60 actual first copy readings in packet-entry order. Afterwards opened exactly M1 native once for the date/hour spacing uncertainties and M2 native once for the hour spacing uncertainty; these did not resolve meaningful spaces versus glyph side bearings, and both readings remain. No crops, substituted assets, generated/edited views, invented opening events or runtime session IDs. Scores judge visible execution; evidence does not assert invisible maker intent. This procedure is my semantic attestation, not a claim that helpers proved visual inspection.

Nevertheless its title/slogan/paragraph/date/hours/place/footer ladder and right-side hand/plant hero proportions recur in M4; its serif-title approach has a softer counterpart in M5.

evidence.location: monochrome photo bands left and gothic copy right
evidence.observation: Root handling and the finished pot communicate a documentary care process, unlike M1's display/macro selection collage. But mirrored placement, similar photo-grid division and the same gothic/sans/serif-number mixture leave the two as related photographic systems rather than strongly independent complete directions.

evidence.location: yellow/purple/orange plant silhouettes with left gothic info stack
evidence.observation: Flat cut-like marks and the two handling gestures produce a forceful graphic mood. The title and serif date are nearly the same type-role treatment as M1; the plant-right/copy-left mass and unchanged logistical grouping repeat M2. It is not just a palette swap, but its full organization is still highly related.

evidence.location: pink botanical cutaway left and delicate serif copy right
evidence.observation: The exposed roots, fine contours and soft shadows supply a specific quiet care subject and a clear contrast with M4's bold plant silhouettes. Its right-column title/Latin/slogan/paragraph/date/hours/place/access/care/invitation/URL ladder, however, is the same repeated system seen in M3 and a mirror of M2. Thin supporting type changes tone more than information organization.

evidence.location: relationship of all five information systems
evidence.observation: All five carry almost the same top-small-market-label, huge-title, Latin-line, bold-or-serif-slogan, ordinary explanatory block, large-serif-date, hours/place and lower practical footer proportions. Shared layouts and text-role order are permitted; the score of 3 reflects the combined recurrence of typographic contrasts, proportional rhythm and generic plant-versus-copy staging after counting actual scene, color, viewpoint and mood differences, not a demand for five unique layouts.

residuals: There is meaningful scene and mood variation: presentation/leaf detail, watering, root handling, plant inspection and cutaway roots. This is more than five color filters, but the repeated complete information-and-hero system prevents a strong five-direction diversity score.
All five remain in the record. Strong local image execution in M2/M3/M4 does not average away M1/M5 typography or the set diversity of 3.
M1 date/hour and M2 hour meaningful-space fidelity remains NA after the permitted single native revisits; no replacement or inferred copy resolves it.
